items.explanation: ぱ is 'pa': は ('ha') with handakuten. The small circle ゜ is called handakuten. It is only used on the H row and turns h into p.
items.mnemonic: は blowing a little bubble ゜: the soft 'h' pops into a 'p', 'pa'.
items.culture_note: かんぱい (乾杯) literally means 'dry cup'. At Japanese gatherings nobody drinks until someone raises a glass and says it.

items.explanation: ぴ is 'pi': ひ ('hi') with handakuten.
items.mnemonic: ひ blowing a little bubble ゜: the soft 'h' pops into a 'p', 'pi'.
items.culture_note: Japanese has thousands of sound-symbolic words like ぴかぴか. Pikachu's name is often explained as ピカ (sparkle) plus チュウ (a mouse's squeak).

items.explanation: ぷ is 'pu': ふ ('fu') with handakuten.
items.mnemonic: ふ blowing a little bubble ゜: the soft 'h' pops into a 'p', 'pu'.

items.explanation: ぺ is 'pe': へ ('he') with handakuten.
items.mnemonic: へ blowing a little bubble ゜: the soft 'h' pops into a 'p', 'pe'.
items.culture_note: ぺこぺこ describes an empty stomach: おなかがぺこぺこ (onaka ga pekopeko) means 'I'm starving'.

items.explanation: ぽ is 'po': ほ ('ho') with handakuten.
items.mnemonic: ほ blowing a little bubble ゜: the soft 'h' pops into a 'p', 'po'.
